tasks.title: Current interference compensation
tasks.statement: CompassMot: at zero throttle `MAG.MagX` = **{b0}** mG, at a current of **{i} A** it is **{b1}** mG (compensation off). Which `COMPASS_MOT_X` value does the firmware save with `COMPASS_MOTCT = 2`, in mG/A?
tasks.solution: `compassmot.cpp`: the interference is ΔB = B − B₀, and the coefficient is MOT = −ΔB / I. The minus sign: in `correct_field` the compensation MOT·I is added to the field and must cancel the interference. If the field dropped with current, the coefficient is positive.

tasks.title: CompassMot interference percentage
tasks.statement: After CompassMot: `COMPASS_MOT_X = {mx}`, `COMPASS_MOT_Y = {my}`, `COMPASS_MOT_Z = {mz}` mG/A; the highest current of the procedure, **{i} A**, was reached at the highest throttle of **{g} %**. Which interference percentage does the procedure show (the reference field in the firmware is 530 mG)?
tasks.solution: `compassmot.cpp`: percentage = |MOT| · (I_max / throttle_max) / 530 · 100, where |MOT| = √(x² + y² + z²), throttle_max is the highest throttle of the procedure from 0 to 1 (the current is scaled to full throttle; at full throttle throttle_max = 1), and 530 mG is `AP_ARMING_COMPASS_MAGFIELD_EXPECTED`. Per the wiki, under 30 % is acceptable, 31–60 % is a gray zone, and above 60 % means move the compass.

tasks.title: Offset vector length and the arming threshold
tasks.statement: After a calibration: `COMPASS_OFS_X = {x}`, `COMPASS_OFS_Y = {y}`, `COMPASS_OFS_Z = {z}`. Find the length of the offset vector in mG: that is what the pre-arm check compares with `COMPASS_OFFS_MAX` (1800 by default).
tasks.solution: `AP_Arming.cpp`: `offsets.length() > get_offsets_max()` → `PreArm: Compass offsets too high`. Length = √(x² + y² + z²). The calibrator, by contrast, checks each offset separately, so a calibration can pass while arming does not: three offsets of 1100 give a length of 1905.

tasks.title: Large Vehicle MagCal: the X axis offset
tasks.statement: The vehicle sits level, true heading **{psi}°**. The model field at the point: north N = **{n}** mG, east E = **{e}** mG. The compass, with no old offsets, shows `MagX` = **{m}** mG. Which `COMPASS_OFS_X` does `MAV_CMD_FIXED_MAG_CAL_YAW` save, in mG?
tasks.solution: `mag_cal_fixed_yaw`: the expected field on the X axis of a level vehicle is X = N·cos ψ + E·sin ψ; offset = expected − measured, because in `correct_field` the offset is added to the measurement.

tasks.title: BATT_VOLT_MULT correction
tasks.statement: `BATT2_VOLT_MULT = {k}`. The ground station shows **{g} V** for monitor 2, and a multimeter on the same battery reads **{m} V**. Find the new `BATT2_VOLT_MULT`.
tasks.solution: `AP_BattMonitor_Analog.cpp`: V = (V_in − `VLT_OFFSET`) × `VOLT_MULT`, so the reading is directly proportional to the multiplier. New = old × reference / reading. A reading below the reference means the multiplier grows.

tasks.title: BATT_AMP_PERVLT correction from the charge
tasks.statement: `BATT_AMP_PERVLT = {k}` A/V, the current zero is set. Over a flight the flight controller counted **{f} mAh**, and the charger put in **{c} mAh**. Find the new `BATT_AMP_PERVLT`.
tasks.solution: I = (V_in − `AMP_OFFSET`) × `AMP_PERVLT`: the current and the accumulated mAh are proportional to the multiplier. New = old × charger mAh / flight controller mAh. First the zero (`BATT_AMP_OFFSET`), then the scale, otherwise the sensor is right at one point only (`ap-setup-scratch`).

tasks.title: The "sum" monitor mask
tasks.statement: Monitor 1 is a sum (`BATT_MONITOR = 10`). It must include monitors **{a}**, **{b}** and **{c}**. Find `BATT_SUM_MASK`.
tasks.solution: `AP_BattMonitor_Sum.cpp`: the check is `_sum_mask & (1 << i)`, where i is the monitor number minus 1. Bit 0 is monitor 1, so monitor n contributes 2^(n − 1). The sum never includes itself; a mask of 0 means "all monitors with a number higher than mine".

tasks.title: Time to BATT_LOW_MAH
tasks.statement: `BATT_CAPACITY = {cap}` mAh, `BATT_LOW_MAH = {low}` mAh. **{used} mAh** are consumed and the current stays at **{i} A**. In how many minutes does the low capacity failsafe trigger?
tasks.solution: `check_failsafe_types`: low on capacity when `CAPACITY` − consumed < `LOW_MAH`. (cap − low − used) mAh remain to the threshold; time = mAh / (I · 1000) hours, times 60. The capacity threshold triggers at once, and `BATT_LOW_TIMER` does not apply to it.

tasks.title: Resting voltage for BATT_FS_VOLTSRC = 1
tasks.statement: The monitor shows **{v} V** at a current of **{i} A**; the resistance estimate `BAT.Res` = **{r} Ω**. Which voltage, in V, does the firmware compare with `BATT_LOW_VOLT` when `BATT_FS_VOLTSRC = 1`?
tasks.solution: `update_resistance_estimate`: V_rest = V + I · R; `voltage_resting_estimate` never returns less than the measured voltage. With source 1 the `BATT_LOW_VOLT` and `BATT_CRT_VOLT` thresholds are compared with this number, so they are set from the no-load voltage.
